Senses.Explanation: Literally, 縮却舌頭 is to draw back the tongue. Xiatang Huiyuan uses it as a direct command: when a monk asks him to speak apart from the four propositions and hundred negations, he tells the monk to draw back his tongue and bring a question. Zhenxie Qingliao similarly raises the line 'empty clarity shines by itself without taxing mental effort,' then says to draw back the tongue and raise something else. An earlier lamp assigns to Wenhui a verse saying that Linji draws back his tongue while Deshan puts away his staff; the later Five Lamps recension places a near-identical verse in Ruiyan Zihong's section. The article retains the earlier lamp witness and records rather than resolves that attribution change. Thus the records use the phrase both in commands that reject the wording just presented and in a paired verse image; they do not supply a separate technical definition for the bodily phrase.
